subject: geography
prompt: Over many years, wind and rain slowly carved a smooth tunnel through a tall limestone cliff by the ocean. Which process most likely created this tunnel?
optionC: Heat and pressure formed new minerals
explanation: Weathering breaks down rock through wind, rain, and ice, and erosion carries the broken pieces away. Together, they slowly wore away the limestone to create the tunnel.
factClaim: Weathering and erosion by water, wind, and ice can carve tunnels and caves through rocks over long periods of time.
factCheckSource: National Geographic, geology science sources confirm water mixed with carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid that dissolves limestone to create caves and tunnels.

subject: general-science
prompt: A farmer plants a vegetable garden near a forest where rabbits live. Rabbits eat many garden vegetables including lettuce, carrots, and beans. Which of the following plants would most likely survive in this garden?
optionA: A plant with bitter-tasting leaves and thorny stems
optionB: A leafy plant with tender, soft leaves and no protection
optionC: A climbing plant with smooth, juicy stems
optionD: A short plant with thin, delicate leaves
explanation: Plants with bitter taste or thorns protect themselves from being eaten by rabbits. Thorns and bad taste discourage animals from eating the plant.
factClaim: Plants with thorns or bitter-tasting leaves are less likely to be eaten by herbivores like rabbits and deer.
factCheckSource: Multiple horticultural sources (Wild Ones, Forrest Keeling Nursery) confirm thorns and bitter compounds are effective plant defenses against herbivores.

subject: general-science
prompt: A school installs panels on its roof to capture energy from the sun and turn it into electricity for the building. What type of energy resource does the sun provide?
explanation: The sun produces energy every day and will do so for billions of years. We can use this energy over and over, which makes it renewable.
factClaim: Solar energy from the sun is renewable because it will continue to be available for billions of years.
factCheckSource: Multiple sources (SolarTechOnline, NRG Clean Power, Britannica) confirm the sun will continue providing energy for billions of years.

subject: geography
prompt: Colorado Springs has a sunny, dry climate with clear skies most days. Seattle, Washington has a cloudy, rainy climate with many overcast days. Which of the following best explains why solar panels in Colorado Springs can generate more electricity than solar panels in Seattle?
optionA: Colorado Springs is at a higher elevation than Seattle
optionB: Colorado Springs has more direct hours of sunshine reaching the panels
optionC: Solar panels work better in cold, dry climates
optionD: Colorado Springs is farther from the Pacific Ocean
explanation: Solar panels need sunlight to generate electricity. Colorado Springs has more sunny days and more hours of direct sunlight, so its panels produce more electricity.
factClaim: Regions with more hours of daily sunlight generate more solar electricity than regions with frequent cloud cover.
factCheckSource: TurbineGenerator.org, SolarPanel.news, and elevation/irradiance studies confirm both cloud cover and elevation contribute to Colorado Springs' solar advantage.

subject: general-science
prompt: A toy uses a hanging weight attached to a string to wind up and spin a propeller, until the weight reaches the ground. Which change would make the propeller spin for a longer time before stopping?
optionC: Releasing the weight from a greater height
optionD: Replacing the weight with a lighter one
explanation: When the weight falls from a greater height, it has more energy to transfer to spinning the propeller. More energy means the propeller spins longer.
factClaim: The greater the height from which an object falls, the more gravitational potential energy it has to do work.
factCheckSource: Physics education sources (Pearson, Lumen Learning, Physics LibreTexts) confirm PE = mgh relationship.

subject: general-science
prompt: A swimmer kicks off from the wall of a pool. As they push hard against the wall in one direction, they move forward through the water in the opposite direction. What caused the swimmer to move?
optionA: The forces pushing on the swimmer were balanced
optionB: The forces pushing on the swimmer were unbalanced
optionC: The force of gravity on the swimmer was equal to the force of the water
optionD: The force of friction was the only force acting on the swimmer
explanation: The swimmer moves because an unbalanced force is pushing them—the push against the wall is stronger than the resistance from the water. Unbalanced forces cause objects to move.
factClaim: Unbalanced forces cause objects to accelerate or change direction.
factCheckSource: Physics Classroom and CK-12 Foundation confirm unbalanced forces cause acceleration per Newton's Second Law.

subject: geography
prompt: A concrete barrier is built to stop flooding. A sand dune is a natural raised bank covered in beach grass and plants. Which of the following is an advantage of using a sand dune instead of a concrete barrier to protect against flooding?
optionA: The sand dune is made from natural materials
optionB: The sand dune is built faster than a concrete barrier
optionC: The sand dune takes up less space than a concrete barrier
optionD: The sand dune requires less maintenance over time
explanation: A sand dune uses natural materials like sand and plants, while a concrete barrier is an artificial structure. Using natural materials can be better for the environment.
factClaim: Natural structures and materials used for flood protection can have environmental advantages over artificial barriers.
factCheckSource: NOAA Coastal Science and New Jersey Sea Grant documentation show dunes reduce wave impact and have environmental benefits; ScienceDirect research shows concrete barriers cause habitat destruction and erosion problems.

subject: general-science
prompt: A bridge can be made from steel, wood, or stone. An engineer wants to know which material makes the strongest bridge. Which of the following is the best way for the engineer to determine which material is strongest?
optionA: The engineer builds one bridge from steel and tests it when a heavy truck crosses
optionB: The engineer asks construction workers which material they prefer to use
optionC: The engineer builds test bridges from each material and compares how much weight each one can hold before breaking
optionD: The engineer measures the temperature and humidity where bridges made from each material are located
explanation: To fairly compare materials, the engineer must test bridges made from each material using the same conditions and measurement method. This is a controlled comparison.
factClaim: To test which of several materials is strongest, you must test samples of each material using identical conditions and measurements.
factCheckSource: ScienceDirect, Britannica, and Xometry confirm material testing requires standardized devices, identical conditions, and consistent measurement protocols.

subject: general-science
prompt: A student mixed sugar into a cup of tea and recorded the temperature, color, and smell before and after mixing. Which of the following questions was the student most likely investigating?
optionB: Did the tea gain stored energy?
optionC: Did a chemical reaction take place?
optionD: How does temperature affect the color of tea?
explanation: A chemical reaction changes the properties of a substance, such as its color, temperature, and smell. By observing these changes, the student was testing whether a chemical reaction happened.
factClaim: Changes in color, temperature, or smell can indicate that a chemical reaction has taken place.
factCheckSource: Chemistry education sources confirm temperature, color, and smell changes are key indicators of chemical reactions.

subject: general-science
prompt: In a scooter, the axle is a metal rod that the wheels are attached to. What is the main function of the axle in a scooter?
optionA: It holds the deck and frame together
optionB: It spins and allows the wheels to turn
optionC: It keeps the scooter body off the ground
optionD: It adds weight to make the scooter more stable
explanation: The axle is a rod that wheels spin around. When you push the scooter forward, the axle rotates, which makes the wheels turn and moves you forward.
factClaim: An axle is a rod that wheels rotate around to make the vehicle move.
factCheckSource: Dictionary.com, Vocabulary.com, and Wikipedia define axle as a rod around which wheels rotate.

subject: general-science
prompt: Long ago, sailors on ships used hand signals and horn sounds to communicate with other ships instead of using radio equipment. Which of the following is an advantage of using hand signals for communication instead of a radio?
optionA: The messages can be sent and received underwater
optionB: Sending the messages is faster than using a radio
optionC: The messages can be sent without needing to speak or share a language
optionD: The messages are secure and cannot be heard by anyone else
explanation: Hand signals can be understood by people who speak different languages because you don't need words. A radio requires speakers to understand the same language.
factClaim: Visual communication methods like hand signals can work across different languages, while spoken communication requires a shared language.
factCheckSource: Multiple sources confirm hand signals and visual communication transcend language barriers; manual communication research shows visual signals are powerful across diverse groups.

subject: general-science
prompt: A wind turbine converts the moving air into electrical energy. Under which of the following conditions will a wind turbine produce the most electrical energy?
optionC: When the wind speed is 8-12 miles per hour
optionD: When the wind speed is 18-25 miles per hour
explanation: Faster winds carry more energy. Wind turbines produce the most electricity when the wind is blowing fastest, because moving air has more kinetic energy to convert.
factClaim: Wind turbines produce more electrical energy when wind speeds are higher.
factCheckSource: Energy Education, Business Norway, and SolarTechOnline confirm wind turbine output increases with wind speed following cubic relationship.

subject: general-science
prompt: A skateboarder rides down a hill, then up the other side. Their speed is 8 miles per hour part way up the hill, 5 miles per hour at the very top of the hill, and 12 miles per hour part way down the other side. A student says that the skateboard has the most kinetic energy when it is at the top of the hill. What evidence shows that this student's claim is incorrect?
optionA: The skateboard must be pushed to go up the hill
optionB: The skateboard has a constant weight at the top of the hill
optionC: The skateboard moves faster part way down the hill than at the top
optionD: The skateboard rolls without friction at the top of the hill
explanation: Kinetic energy depends on how fast an object is moving. The skateboard is moving faster (12 mph) part way down than at the top (5 mph), so it has more kinetic energy going down.
factClaim: Kinetic energy increases with speed; an object moving faster has more kinetic energy than the same object moving slower.
factCheckSource: Physics education sources confirm KE = ½mv² relationship, showing kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity.

subject: general-science
prompt: A metal rail runs along a subway platform. If lightning were to strike the rail, it must safely conduct electricity away from people and into the ground. What material should be used for this conductive rail?
explanation: Metal conducts electricity well and allows it to flow safely to the ground. Plastic, rubber, and ceramic are insulators—they block electricity and keep it from flowing.
factClaim: Metals conduct electricity, while plastic, rubber, and ceramic are insulators that do not conduct electricity.
factCheckSource: Study.com, Scientific American, and CK-12 Foundation confirm metals conduct electricity while plastic, rubber, and ceramics are insulators.

subject: general-science
prompt: Two rabbits with brown fur and long ears are bred together and have baby rabbits. One parent rabbit was trained to hop through a tunnel at a young age, and the other parent learned to come when called—things they were taught, not born knowing. Which of the following is a trait the baby rabbits would most likely inherit from their parents?
optionB: The ability to hop through a tunnel
optionD: The skill to find food quickly
explanation: Fur color is inherited—it comes from the parents' genes. Trained behaviors like hopping through tunnels or coming when called must be learned; they are not passed down genetically.
factClaim: Physical traits like fur color and body shape are inherited from parents through genes, while behaviors like tricks and commands must be learned.
factCheckSource: Multiple education sources distinguish inherited traits (genetic) from learned behaviors (acquired through experience); examples include eye color inherited vs. skills learned.
